attempted_claim: Let d=q+1 with q a prime power (e.g. d=6) and let G be a non-bipartite d-regular Ramanujan graph from the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak / Morgenstern arithmetic family. Does G admit an edge-signing sigma:E(G)->{+-1} whose signed adjacency matrix A_sigma satisfies rho(A_sigma) <= 2*sqrt(d-1), equivalently a 2-lift H all of whose new eigenvalues lie in [-2*sqrt(d-1), 2*sqrt(d-1)] so that H is itself d-regular Ramanujan?
decisive_failure: Exhaustive signing search was verified only on small cubic Ramanujan graphs (n<=10) and heuristic search on random 6-regular Ramanujan proxies at n=20/30; no explicit LPS/Morgenstern graph at genuine scale (n>=60, m>=180) was constructed or certified, and no literature retrieval was consumed. The blocking diagnosis rests on the one-sided versus two-sided interlacing gap plus exponential scaling, not on a discovered counterexample.
